question: what are the unresolved references a corpus reports, and is any of them a resolution defect

corpus.note: symbols and unresolved counted off the published canonical graph, not off the index event

CRATE_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND.what: the sysroot and external crates -- alloc, core, std and dependencies the local cache did not fetch
CRATE_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND.verdict: declared limitation: Rust indexing is hermetic by default

impl_blocks.what: inherent and trait impl blocks -- `impl::Type` and `impl::Type::Trait` -- which the loader never publishes as symbols
impl_blocks.evidence: find_symbol with kind=implementation over rs-svc-a answers total 0, while the members of those same blocks are indexed and appear in get_file_outline
impl_blocks.verdict: a reference that can never resolve, against a kind the loader has code to render and never creates

derived_trait_members.verdict: inherent absence: there is no source occurrence to index

tail.what: two tuple fields spelled `::0` and one bare test function name

limitations: one corpus, one machine, one toolchain. A different sysroot or a fetched dependency moves the 94.3 % bucket
the classification of the 112 is by symbol shape, read label by label; every label is quoted in the report so a reader can disagree with the reading

the probe reads the canonical graph, so its per-language symbol counts are the graph's, which do not match the index event's go_definitions -- one counts published symbols and the other counts definitions the loader saw
all three languages are classified now, each over one corpus and one toolchain; another sysroot, other cached dependencies or a built workspace moves all three splits

observations_versus_facts.what: the per-language counters in the index event count observations; the canonical graph stores distinct facts, keyed by file, reason, requested package, requested symbol and start offset
observations_versus_facts.why: with tests on, go/packages loads pkg and pkg.test and both observe the same position in the same file
observations_versus_facts.verdict: no row is lost; the number a user reads overstates distinct facts by 1.58x on this corpus. LUQUE-2009

DECLARATION_OUTSIDE_REPOSITORY.what: the *.test packages the Go toolchain synthesises inside the build cache
DECLARATION_OUTSIDE_REPOSITORY.evidence: every detail is a path under Library/Caches/go-build/

PACKAGE_NOT_BUILDABLE.what: directories whose Go files are all behind build tags
PACKAGE_NOT_BUILDABLE.evidence: detail reads `build constraints exclude all Go files in ...`

PROVIDER_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.what: workspace's own packages, none of which has a dist/

DECLARATION_NOT_RESOLVED.what: a name the provider does not declare

internal_share.what: occurrences asking for workspace's own packages rather than third-party ones
internal_share.corpus_state: verified: none of sdk-module-ts, library-web or library-shared has a dist/

what_a_build_would_fix.answer: nothing. Every internal package is a workspace member, all 105 @workspace/* declarations across 28 package.json files pin 0.0.1 rather than workspace:*, and pnpm 11 defaults link-workspace-packages to false. So every consumer resolves its own monorepo's packages from published tarballs in the store, which carry no src and no .d.ts.map, and the loader excludes installed copies by design
what_a_build_would_fix.measured: library-web was pulled, built with nine .d.ts.map files, and the corpus went from 5998 unresolved to 5997
what_a_build_would_fix.what_would_fix_it: consumers resolving the workspace copy: link-workspace-packages=true, or the 105 ranges as workspace:*. Both are decisions about their dependency tree

resolved_after_linking.change: linkWorkspacePackages: true in pnpm-workspace.yaml -- not .npmrc, where pnpm 10+ no longer reads its own settings -- then reinstall and build the five internal packages
resolved_after_linking.what_remains: 463, still naming @workspace/sdk, and inherent: the sdk re-exports SlashCommandBuilder and Collection from @discordjs/builders and @discordjs/collection, so the declaring source leaves the corpus. Same class as the Rust sysroot

corrections.what: the first version of this report read declarationMap out of the three tsconfig.json files and concluded @workspace/web did not emit one
corrections.why_it_was_wrong: library-web builds with tsdown, not tsc, and its tsdown.config.ts carries dts: { sourcemap: true }
corrections.how_it_was_caught: the user said the library should have a map; pulling and building it produced nine .d.ts.map files, and re-measuring showed the unresolved count did not move
corrections.what_replaced_it: the measured explanation: consumers resolve @workspace/web from a published tarball, and the loader excludes installed copies by design

corrections.what: this report then claimed library-web was absent from pnpm-workspace.yaml
corrections.why_it_was_wrong: the file has 43 entries and library-web is line 24; the claim came from reading it through head -3
corrections.how_it_was_caught: editing the file to add the entry produced a duplicate, which showed the original was already there
corrections.what_replaced_it: one cause for the whole internal bucket: workspace members consumed as published tarballs because nothing links them
